title: Vivarium Civilisation
blurb: The flagship. Thousands of agents on a planetary surface, each with needs, movement, resource use and reproduction, all updated every tick. This is the workload the engine exists for: many entities, small components, nothing sitting idle.

title: Murmuration
blurb: Up to eight million real ECS entities, each with its own component row, steered by a shared flow field and moved on the CPU in Rust/WASM. JavaScript never copies a single instance — the renderer takes a raw pointer into the archetype's transform column and hands it straight to the GPU. A GPU-compute mode runs the identical field for a direct comparison.
meta: zero-copy bridge · dense iteration · CPU vs. GPU

title: Bouncing Rects
blurb: The smallest possible fully GPU-driven scene: no per-rect ECS entity and no per-rect CPU work at all. Every rect lives in a GPU storage buffer, is spawned by a compute shader from its own instance index, and is drawn in one instanced call. Changing the count changes one float.
meta: GPU-driven · compute shaders · zero CPU cost

title: Scheduler
blurb: A recording of the engine's own update schedule: one row per system, timed on the rayon workers themselves. Systems share a stage only when their declared reads and writes are disjoint, so every barrier is a real data conflict. Flip to one core and watch the stages turn into a staircase.

title: Metamorphosis
blurb: Three optional components make eight signatures, so the engine builds eight archetypes — one per corner of a cube, one component per axis. Every cube crossing an edge is a row being physically moved between tables. Turn the churn up and watch what that costs.
meta: archetype migration · structural change · query filters
